chapter_title: [Concerning the Four Fathers; what they are like.]
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly core correspondential teaching: a systematic body→cosmos mapping (hidden/visible organs ↔ hidden/visible divine realities; eyes ↔ light-ships; tongue ↔ Jesus the Splendour). The only clear late layer is the dialogue attribution in ¶1 (frame) and the concluding summarizing flourish in ¶9 (frame-style closure). No NT citation formulae or institutional/pastoral grafts appear.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as the corporeal body has limbs that are hidden, so it also has others that are visible. They can be seen upon it, they can be grasped and receive blows and wounds, whilst others can neither be grasped nor receive blows.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:" (layer-2 hagiographic framing marker; "apostle" attribution is not part of the substrate teaching).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The teaching itself is impersonal correspondential exposition (body visibility/invisibility as an ontological template). The only late signal is the explicit speaker-attribution frame formula.

paragraphs.core_text: So it is also with this entire greatness, as we resemble it. Some of it is hidden, whilst some of it is visible; some of it is far away from the blows and suffering, whilst some of it receives blows and wounds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmos/body analogy continuing the structural mapping (hidden/visible; impassible/passible) without audience exhortation, institutions, or citations.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, thus the directive of the body that lives within, hidden in the storehouses inside the body and unseen. So it is also how the Father, the God of truth, exists; as he too is hidden in his kingdom, not displayed before this outer desolation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential mapping stays within the cosmic system: inner directive faculty ↔ Father hidden in his kingdom; impersonal explanatory voice and cosmological naming (Father, kingdom).

paragraphs.core_text: Thus, too, the body has two eyes that are visible and seen, and are even the body's source of illumination; so there are also these two light ships that shine and are seen in the entire universe and the whole of creation. The light has never been hidden, just like the two eyes of the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic correspondential equation (eyes ↔ two light ships) with cosmic geography (universe/creation) and no institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The living soul too is like this; it is established in apparent silence. In its apparent silence it is grasped and receives blows from these five fleshes, which destroy (the soul) and strike it. It can be likened to the mystery of the corporeal body, as it can be grasped and mastered, can receive blows and wounds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mythic mechanics: the living soul as a passible entity struck by the five fleshes; correspondential comparison remains cosmos↔body, not cosmos↔contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.152⟩ Also, thus this tongue that speaks, proclaims, reprimands and reveals about everything happening in this body, inside and outside, also the considerations and bodily knowledges. The tongue, which is outside, makes it manifest. It also proclaims about the honour and shame of the body. And it speaks, unveiling the pain of the body that is sick from its sores.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal functional description of an organ/faculty preparing the next correspondence (tongue ↔ revealer). No frame/citation cues; remains structural.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also what Jesus the Splendour is like, who shall be sent from the greatness. He manifests and reveals about everything, both the external and the internal, both what is above and what is below. Be it about the outer aeons that are hidden and not displayed, or about the ships of light that are seen: he is the one who unveils about them. He is also the one who reveals about their glory, and the greatness that dwells in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus the Splendour functions as a named cosmological entity in a systematic role (revealer like the tongue). Despite Christian vocabulary, there is no NT entry vector (no Gospel quotation), so it reads as Manichaean cosmological substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: And regarding this beating and wounding of the living soul, Jesus is the one who reveals it. He also preaches about (the soul) and its peace. He reveals about its cleansing and healing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same cosmic correspondence (revealer making known the soul’s suffering and restoration). The verb "preaches" does not introduce a Gospel citation or ecclesial rule here; it remains within the mythic-cosmological system.
Closing summary in demonstrative/authorial voice ("Behold, I have shown to you...") functions as editorial wrap-up rather than substrate exposition.
